事下中書，光允謂崇韜曰：「復恭與山南謀逆，顯當國法，本朝未經昭雪，安得論理？」

repairs.before: The matter was sent down to the Secretariat, and Guangyun said to Chongyao, "Fu Gong plotted rebellion with Shannan and clearly deserved the national law; the present dynasty has not yet cleared his name—how can his case be argued?"
repairs.after: The matter was sent down to the Secretariat, and Guangyun said to Chongtao, "Fugong plotted rebellion with Shannan and clearly deserved the national law; the present dynasty has not yet cleared his name—how can his case be argued?"
repairs.reason: 郭崇韜: 韜 is tāo; the record's own pinyin is Guō Chóngtāo and accepted idiomatic repairs r0004/r0005/r0007 already read Chongtao. 復恭 is one given name, written as Fuguang (復光) is in s0043; splitting it as "Fu Gong" misreads it as surname plus name. Consistency repair.

repairs.after: Zhang Quanyi spoke to Guo Chongtao about restoring him as chief minister; soon afterward he entered court as Guest of the Heir Apparent.

repairs.before: He had three sons—Ji, Song, and Shouzhen. Only Song served the present dynasty, rising to left remonstrating censor-in-chief and ending his career as acting military commissioner of Fu Prefecture.
repairs.after: He had three sons—Qi, Song, and Shouzhen. Only Song served the present dynasty, rising to left remonstrating censor and ending his career as military adjutant (xingjun sima) of Fu Prefecture.
repairs.reason: 頎 is qí. 左諫議大夫 is the remonstrating official rendered "remonstrating censor" in s0116, not a censor-in-chief; 行軍司馬 is the military adjutant, not an acting military commissioner.

repairs.before: His sons Ji, Song, and Shouzhen—only Song served the present dynasty, reaching Left Remonstrating Censor-in-Chief, and ending as Acting Military Commissioner of Fu Prefecture.

repairs.reason: 頎 is qí; 左諫議大夫 is not a censor-in-chief; 行軍司馬 is the military adjutant.
